root_cause.text: ext4_mb_release() only flushed `sbi->s_discard_work` when `EXT4_MOUNT_DISCARD` was still set, so a remount from `discard` to `nodiscard` could leave queued discard work and `s_discard_list` pending during teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` guard and makes `flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work);` and `WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&sbi->s_discard_list));` run unconditionally, matching the CVE description that remounting with `nodiscard` cleared the flag but did not cancel or flush already queued discard work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always drain and validate discard work during ext4 multiblock allocator teardown to avoid stale asynchronous discard activity.
intent_record.what: The DISCARD option check around the discard-work cleanup was removed in ext4_mb_release(), so flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work) and WARN_ON_ONCE(!list_empty(&sbi->s_discard_list)) now execute unconditionally instead of only when test_opt(sb, DISCARD) is true.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ext4 will always wait for pending discard work to finish and verify the discard list is empty during multiblock allocator release, even on filesystems not mounted with DISCARD enabled. This prevents teardown from proceeding while discard-related work may still be active.

grouping_result.intent: Always drain and validate discard work during ext4 multiblock allocator teardown to avoid stale asynchronous discard activity.

relevance_review.reason: The group explicitly changes ext4 multiblock allocator teardown to always drain discard work, which directly matches the root cause of stale queued discard work remaining after remount from discard to nodiscard.

candidates.rationale: This conditional gates the teardown flush on the DISCARD mount option. If the filesystem was remounted from discard to nodiscard, the condition is false and pending discard work is not drained, leaving stale asynchronous discard activity and a non-empty discard list during teardown.

This is the operation that should drain queued discard work during allocator teardown. Because it was executed only under the DISCARD check, it could be skipped after a discard-to-nodiscard remount, allowing queued work to survive teardown.

This check shows the code expected the discard list to be empty after flushing, but it was also conditionally skipped. If discard work remained queued, teardown could proceed with a stale non-empty discard list.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition incorrectly makes teardown of discard work depend on the current DISCARD mount option. After a remount from discard to nodiscard, it prevents flushing queued discard work, leaving stale asynchronous discard activity and a pending discard list.

This is the actual drain of queued discard work, but it was placed behind the DISCARD check. As a result, it could be skipped during teardown after a discard-to-nodiscard remount, allowing pending work to survive.
This sanity check assumes the discard list has been drained, but because it was also conditionally skipped, teardown could proceed without validating that the discard list was empty.
